working_title: Northern Ireland's Causeway Coast Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal Portrush, Portstewart, Castlerock and Ballycastle
angle: Most UK golfers know Royal Portrush exists but treat the Causeway Coast as a one-course destination. This post makes the case for a 3-to-4-day circuit built around the cluster of serious links courses within a short drive of each other, covering the practicalities of getting there from mainland Britain by ferry, where to base yourself, and how to sequence the courses sensibly.
research_notes:
- Royal Portrush (founded 1888) sits on the North Antrim Causeway Coast, approximately 60 miles north-west of Belfast. It has two courses: the Dunluce Links (championship, par 72) and the Valley Links (par 71). It is the only club in Ireland to have hosted The Open Championship; most recently 2019.
- Portstewart Golf Club offers three courses. The Strand Course is an 18-hole championship links, par 72, with a front nine through towering dunes that is widely regarded among the best in Ireland. A Riverside Course (par 68, 18 holes) and an Old Course (par 64) provide alternatives for different days or abilities.
- Castlerock Golf Club: the Mussenden Course is an 18-hole championship links, par 73. The Bann Course is a 9-hole links (par 68 over 18 holes). Both courses are true links running through dunes where the River Bann meets the sea. Castlerock was founded in 1901. It features in UK & Ireland Top 100 rankings. Castlerock is a short drive west of Portstewart — all three (Royal Portrush, Portstewart, Castlerock) are within easy range of each other on the same stretch of coast.
- Ballycastle Golf Club (founded 1890, par 71, 5,876 yards): a hybrid of parkland and links, climbing to elevated ground with views across to Rathlin Island, Fair Head, the Mull of Kintyre and the Glens of Antrim. Located about 20 minutes east of Royal Portrush. Semi-private, open to visitors.
- Bushfoot Golf Club: 9-hole course near Bushmills, links and parkland mix, suits a half-day or warm-up round.
- Three Major champions have lived in the area: Fred Daly, Darren Clarke, and Graeme McDowell — a useful framing detail without fabricating quotes.
- Getting there from mainland Britain: Stena Line (Belfast–Cairnryan, approx. 2 hours); P&O Ferries (Larne–Cairnryan, approx. 2 hours, multiple daily sailings); Stena Line (Belfast–Birkenhead/Liverpool, approx. 8 hours, day and overnight options). Cairnryan–Larne is the shortest crossing from Scotland and convenient for heading straight up the Antrim coast. Train option: Belfast Grand Central to Coleraine (approx. 1 hour 20 minutes, trains run hourly); Coleraine to Portrush by train also possible — but a hire car is strongly advisable to move between golf clubs.
- The train from Belfast to Coleraine has been described as a scenic journey in its own right, passing close to Mussenden Temple on the cliff.
- Visitor tee-time access: Royal Portrush visitor access is limited and typically requires booking through a golf travel company well in advance, especially for Dunluce. Portstewart, Castlerock, and Ballycastle are more accessible to independent visitors but peak-season booking ahead is recommended.
- Base: Portrush or Portstewart are both practical bases. Castlerock is a short drive west; Ballycastle around 20 minutes east.
